sources.entry: Feeds Fun - News reader with tags, scoring, and AI. (Source Code) BSD-3-Clause Python

summary.one_liner: Feeds Fun is a self-hostable news reader that automatically tags feed entries (largely via LLMs) and lets you score, filter, and sort news by those tags.
summary.what_it_does: Feeds Fun loads and parses RSS/Atom-style feeds and assigns tags to every news entry. Tags come from several processors, including simple ones (domain, native feed tags, uppercase titles) and an LLM processor that uses OpenAI or Google Gemini (or OpenAI-compatible/Gemini-compatible third-party models) to detect tags. Users write rules that score news by tags, and can exclude or require tags, then sort by score, date, and similar criteria. The app tracks which items have been read. It has improved handling for Reddit, GitHub, YouTube, ArXiv and Hacker News sources through integration plugins. The backend runs as an ASGI API server plus separate loader and librarian workers; the frontend is a static site built from the feeds-fun NPM package. The README also mentions a cleaner command for pruning old entries and single- and multi-user setups.
use_cases: read only the most important news from many feeds
auto-tag RSS entries with an LLM
score and filter news by topic tags
run a multi-user feed reader for a group
track which news items have been read
how_to_run: npm install feeds-fun && npm install --prefix ./node_modules/feeds-fun && npm run build-only --prefix ./node_modules/feeds-fun (then copy dist to static host)
notable: Tag-based scoring and filtering rules, rather than keyword-only filtering
LLM tag processors support OpenAI, Gemini, and third-party OpenAI-compatible endpoints
Pluggable integrations for specific sources such as Reddit, GitHub, YouTube, ArXiv, Hacker News
Tag normalizer chain that merges variants like 'a-book-review' and splits 'google-vs-microsoft'
Separate loader and librarian workers keep the API server lightweight
caveats: Full tagging power requires an OpenAI or Gemini API key (or a compatible third-party LLM endpoint)
Setup involves PostgreSQL, a SpaCy model download, separate workers, and cron for cleanup; not a one-click install
Upgrades must follow CHANGELOG migration order, keeping backend and frontend versions in sync
README describes many features as still in development and tag normalization as actively changing
